items.title: Challenges and opportunities in using digital health technologies for decision-making in prehospital non-emergency situations in Norway: a qualitative study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Norway has a well-established emergency care system and prehospital infrastructure. However, an ageing population and the increasing prevalence of chronic diseases create a growing need to explore how digital health technologies may support decision-making in prehospital non-emergency situations. While technologies such as telehealth, remote monitoring, wearables, portable medical devices, communication platforms, and Artificial Intelligence-based decision-support systems have shown promise for supporting prehospital decision-making, their implementation in Norway remains limited. This study explored Norwegian paramedics’ perceptions of the challenges and opportunities of using digital health technologies to support decision-making in prehospital non-emergency situations. Methods An exploratory qualitative interview study was conducted to investigate paramedics’ experiences and perceptions of digital health technology use in decision-making during prehospital non-emergency situations in Norway. Data were collected through 12 semi-structured interviews with paramedics involved in Norwegian ambulance care. Participants were recruited using purposive and snowball sampling. Interviews were audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework. NVivo 15 and Microsoft Excel were used to support data organization and analysis. Results Four themes captured challenges and opportunities of digital health technologies in prehospital non-emergency situations: digital support for call assessment and ambulance resource allocation; digital patient information for shared situational awareness; digital communication for interprofessional consultation and care coordination; and digital diagnostics for conveyance and non-conveyance decisions. Participants reported fragmented information systems, restricted access to patient records, limitations in communication technologies, and insufficient diagnostic support. They identified opportunities involving video-supported assessment, interoperable patient information, real-time clinical data sharing, multiparty consultation, and point-of-care diagnostics. However, the perceived value of these technologies depended on their reliability, usability, and integration with professional roles and healthcare services. Conclusions Digital health technologies were perceived as having the potential to support decision-making in prehospital non-emergency situations by reducing uncertainty and supporting appropriate care pathways. Their perceived value depended on reliable information, interoperability, usable communication, diagnostic support, and clear cross-service responsibilities. Digital transformation should therefore prioritise integrated, context-sensitive systems that augment paramedics’ professional judgement and may enable timely, coordinated, and patient-centred care while remaining responsive to evolving clinical needs and care environments.

items.title: Changes in How Humans Think, Relate, and Create in the Age of AI
items.abstract: This chapter traces how knowledge in the technological age has shifted from external systems of storage and retrieval toward generative processes enabled by artificial intelligence. This transition has allowed AI to move beyond managing information and into influencing meaning-making, relationship, and creativity. Using art therapy as a central lens, a field grounded in embodied and relational ways of knowing and creating, the authors draw on a biopsychosocial perspective, developmental neuroscience, and emerging research on AI-assisted tools to examine how the immediacy of contemporary technologies may affect creative cognition, mental health, and the bottom-up processes that support therapeutic change. The chapter emphasizes that protecting client agency, engagement, and self-efficacy requires careful consideration of when and how AI is incorporated into therapeutic contexts.

items.title: Changes in the acceptance of artificial intelligence in medicine among physicians and the general public in Japan: A repeated cross-sectional comparison of 2018 and 2025
items.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) has advanced rapidly, yet whether growing societal familiarity with AI is accompanied by greater willingness to receive relatively autonomous AI-led care remains unclear. We conducted repeated cross-sectional online surveys in Japan in 2018 and 2025 using the same questionnaire and compared self-identified physicians and members of the general public (2018: 399 physicians and 600 members of the public; 2025: 300 physicians and 300 members of the public). Mean responses to the item assessing intention to use medical AI did not differ significantly between survey years in either group, despite consistently favorable evaluations of its usefulness and future necessity. Among physicians, the unadjusted mean response regarding the potential of medical AI to improve clinical efficiency was higher in 2025, but this difference was not significant after adjustment for age and sex. Among members of the public, self-rated knowledge of medical AI was higher in 2025, while expectations that medical AI would increase healthcare costs were also greater. These findings suggest that increased self-rated knowledge may not necessarily be accompanied by greater intention to use relatively autonomous medical AI. Implementation strategies should therefore address concerns regarding responsibility, safety, data protection, and healthcare costs alongside efforts to improve public understanding.

items.title: ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning in the era of generative AI: A bibliometric analysis of research trends, collaboration networks, and emerging pedagogical themes
items.abstract: Purpose – This study aims to map the development of research on ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning during the 2023–2025 period. Methodology – This study uses bibliometric analysis to examine the intellectual, social, and conceptual structures of research on ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning. Data were obtained from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix Biblioshiny. Document selection followed the PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines as a checklist for the identification, screening, eligibility, and inclusion stages. Of the 1,227 documents identified, 143 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed further. Findings – The number of publications increased from 12 in 2023 to 36 in 2024 and 95 in 2025, indicating an annual growth rate of 181.37% and an average of 18.63 citations per document. International co-authorship accounted for only 16.78% of these documents, indicating limited cross-national collaboration. ChatGPT, mathematics education, and artificial intelligence were the most dominant keywords, while geometry, prospective mathematics teachers, and personalized learning were relatively underrepresented. Novelty – Unlike previous studies that generally treat ChatGPT as part of generative artificial intelligence, this research analytically positions ChatGPT-assisted mathematics learning as a separate bibliometric unit and proposes AI-mediated mathematics learning as a conceptual proposition that emphasizes critical validation of AI-generated results. Significance – These findings provide an evidence-based research agenda to strengthen international collaboration and develop mathematics instruction that emphasizes reasoning, justification, and critical evaluation of AI-generated solutions, while identifying priorities for future empirical research.

items.title: Climate Change and Workers’ Health and Safety: An Umbrella Review
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: This umbrella review synthesizes current evidence on the health and safety impacts of climate change among workers. In particular, it aims to identify the main workers' categories at the highest risk, the main health and safety outcomes, methodological limitations, and future directions reported in the literature, as well as preventive strategies described in recent reviews. METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Systematic and scoping reviews addressing climate-related occupational health and safety outcomes were included. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by two reviewers. Methodological quality was assessed using the ROBIS tool, and findings were synthesized in accordance with PRISMA and PRIOR guidelines. RESULTS: Most of the available evidence concerns outdoor occupations, particularly agriculture and construction, where exposure to high temperatures is associated with increased risks of injuries and heat strain. Emerging data also highlight links with mental health, renal disease, and chronic conditions. However, the literature remains fragmented, with few meta-analyses and substantial heterogeneity. Preventive strategies have been proposed, but their implementation remains inconsistent. CONCLUSIONS: Evidence confirms that climate change has become a determinant of occupational health and safety. Future research should strengthen methodological coherence, adopt longitudinal approaches, and address vulnerable populations.

items.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases
items.abstract: Abstract Introduction RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death. Content This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning. Summary Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs. Outlook Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.

items.title: Collaborative Innovation Ecosystems and AI Disruption in Travel and Hospitality
items.abstract: The travel industry is undergoing a massive transformation fueled by Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the increasing number of technology start-ups in the innovation ecosystem. This chapter explores the impact that AI-driven startups are having on the traditional models of travel planning and booking, mobility and hospitality. It looks at the structural characteristics of innovation ecosystems, the importance of venture capital and the rise of “platform” business models based on machine learning, the processing of natural language and the analysis of huge amounts of data. The chapter explores implications for existing travel companies, consumer attitudes, regulations, and sustainable tourism objectives in the context of AI disruption. The chapter brings theory and empirical examples together to improve the understanding of the impact of collaborative innovation ecosystems on the competitive landscape of global travel.

items.title: Comparative evaluation of machine learning algorithms for Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease detection under class imbalance
items.abstract: Maize Lethal Necrosis Disease (MLND) remains a major threat to maize production in sub-Saharan Africa, creating a need for accurate, interpretable, and computationally efficient diagnostic tools. This study presents a comprehensive comparative evaluation of nine machine learning algorithms for MLND detection using a structured feature-based dataset comprising 7,892 maize leaf observations obtained from the Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO). The extracted features captured color, texture, lesion, and morphological characteristics associated with MLND symptoms. To address moderate class imbalance, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and class weighting were incorporated within the model development pipeline, and their contribution was quantified through an ablation study. Model performance was evaluated using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation, an independent 80/20 test set, and leave-one-county-out cross-validation (LOCO-CV) to assess geographic generalisability. Across repeated cross-validation, the leading models demonstrated consistent predictive performance with narrow 95% confidence intervals. CatBoost achieved the highest mean accuracy (0.753; 95% CI: 0.730–0.773), while Logistic Regression attained the highest mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.808; 95% CI: 0.787–0.830). The overlapping confidence intervals among the best-performing models indicate broadly comparable predictive performance, highlighting the importance of considering complementary criteria beyond accuracy alone. LOCO-CV demonstrated minimal performance variation across counties, indicating good internal geographic generalisability. Calibration analysis using Expected Calibration Error (ECE) showed that post-hoc probability calibration substantially improved the reliability of predicted probabilities. At the same time, explainable artificial intelligence techniques consistently identified Chlorosis Intensity, Green–Yellow Ratio, and Necrotic Area as the most influential predictors. Considering predictive performance alongside computational efficiency, model size, and inference latency, LightGBM provided the most favorable balance for resource-constrained environments. In contrast, Logistic Regression offered a highly interpretable alternative with minimal computational requirements. Although the achieved performance indicates that approximately one in four samples may be misclassified and further external validation is required before operational deployment, the findings demonstrate that structured feature-based machine learning provides a transparent, computationally efficient, and interpretable framework for MLND detection and establishes a strong foundation for future field-based decision-support systems.

items.title: Comparison of Diagnostic Accuracy Between Artificial Intelligence vs. Clinical Examination in Maxillofacial Pathologies Among Pediatric Patients
items.abstract: Background: The diagnosis of pediatric maxillofacial pathologies requires precise timing and planning of treatment.Though several studies have been conducted to assess the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the diagnostic support of oral and maxillofacial pathologies and diseases, the role of AI in routine practice compared to clinical examination still needs to be investigated, especially in the pediatric population.Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of AI in comparison with clinical examination in detecting maxillofacial pathologies in the pediatric population.Methods: A cross-sectional study performed on 120 pediatric patients between the ages of 6 and 15 years.Data were collected using a structured Pediatric Maxillofacial Clinical Examination Form, an AIbased Diagnostic Assessment Form, and a Standardized Radiographic Assessment Proforma.The clinical and AI-based diagnoses were compared to the final diagnosis made through an appropriate combination of supplementary clinical, radiological, and histopathological assessments.The measurements of the diagnostic performances were sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values and overall diagnostic accuracy.Results: AI-based assessment yielded an overall diagnostic accuracy of 90.8%.It was also sensitive (90.3%) and specific (91.7%) in comparison to clinical examination which had an overall diagnostic accuracy of 79.2% (sensitivity: 79.2%, specificity: 79.2%).Positive and negative predictive values of AI assessments were significantly greater than of clinical examination.Conclusion: In the present study, AI assessment demonstrated higher diagnostic performance than clinical examination in the examined pediatric population.AI could be deployed as an aide in diagnosis of maxillofacial pathologies, however, clinicians must rely on their clinical expertise and performserial investigations to provide the final diagnosis.

items.title: Computational Mechanisms of the AI Placebo Effect: A Bayesian Re-Analysis of Expectation-Driven Performance in Human–Computer Interaction
items.abstract: The AI placebo effect, whereby the mere belief in artificial intelligence assistance alters userexpectations and task performance, is an established phenomenon in human-computer interaction(HCI). Yet the cognitive mechanisms linking placebo beliefs to objective behavioural outcomes remainpoorly understood. This study applies a hierarchical Bayesian computational framework to re-analysedata from Kosch et al. (2022, Experiment 2; N = 75), in which participants completed a word puzzletask under either a Control condition (no AI belief) or an AI Placebo condition (belief in sham AIassistance). We compared three models in which the AI placebo manipulation altered either (a) themean of a prior performance expectation distribution (Shift model), (b) the precision (inverse variance)of that distribution (Precision model), or (c) both simultaneously (Combined model). Bayesian modelcomparison via Leave-One-Out cross-validation strongly favoured the Combined model(elpd_diff = 7.11 over the next-best model). Despite the winning model, group-level analyses revealedno statistically reliable average shift in either prior mean or precision due to the placebo manipulation(95% HDIs broadly overlapping zero), mirroring the null group-level performance effect reported byKosch et al. Crucially, at the individual level, the estimated change in prior mean shift was stronglyand positively correlated with observed performance improvement (r = 0.973, p < .0001), explaining theindividual-level expectancy–performance relationship originally observed. Unexpectedly, reduced priorprecision (not increased precision) was associated with greater performance gains under the placebo(r = 0.595, p < .0001). These findings provide the first demonstration that hierarchical Bayesian modelsoriginally developed to explain placebo analgesia can successfully account for individual differences inthe AI placebo effect on objective task performance. The results indicate that the cognitive mechanisminvolves simultaneous modulation of both expectation level and expectation certainty, yet manifestshighly heterogeneously across participants. We discuss implications for theories of expectancy-drivenperformance and for HCI evaluation methodology.

items.title: Computational Peptide Design: Emerging Concepts in Antibiotics, Immunity, and Evolution
items.abstract: Peptides are among the smallest functional biomolecules. Learning to systematically design their activity would revolutionize biology and medicine. Yet achieving this goal remains an open challenge. Recent advances in machine learning enable the discovery and design of peptides at scale, not only yielding new antibiotic agents effective against priority pathogens but also revealing unexpected roles for peptides in host immunity. In this review, we survey how artificial intelligence (AI) methods can be used to mine genomes, proteomes, and even ancient sequence data to uncover “encrypted” peptide antibiotics across the tree of life and over evolutionary time. We highlight emerging approaches for activity prediction, structure–activity modeling, sequence optimization, and de novo peptide generation, and we discuss workflows that tightly couple in silico design with high-throughput experimental validation. We further introduce the concept of “encrypted immunity,” in which ordinary proteins encode latent antimicrobial fragments, and we outline translational opportunities as well as remaining challenges on the path to bringing AI-designed peptides to the clinic.

items.title: Constrained LLM-Guided Model Selection for Cross-Chemistry Early-Life Battery Prognostics
items.abstract: Data-driven battery prognostics can fail when models trained on one chemistry are deployed on another. This study investigates early-life end-of-life (EOL) classification under chemistry-driven domain shift and introduces a schema-constrained large language model (LLM) configuration layer as the primary methodological contribution. The LLM does not predict EOL directly and does not introduce a new transfer-learning or uncertainty-estimation algorithm. Instead, it maps structured chemistry context and numerical dataset evidence to an executable architecture, reliability head, and bounded set of training hyperparameters selected from an approved model zoo containing one-dimensional CNN, self-attention, WideResNet, OpenMax, and Spectral-normalized Neural Gaussian Process (SNGP) options. Full degradation trajectories define five EOL categories using an 80% state-of-health threshold, whereas model inputs are restricted to early-cycle observations. Across six directed Argonne/CAMP chemistry-transfer tasks, the target-only deterministic CNN achieved a mean balanced accuracy of 68.9%, compared with 78.3% for the LLM-selected CNN with self-attention and SNGP, corresponding to an average improvement of 9.4 percentage points. Fixed non-LLM transfer alternatives achieved 70.0% for the deterministic CNN, 71.7% for the OpenMax-enforced CNN, 66.5% for deterministic WideResNet, and 73.3% for WideResNet-SNGP. Context ablation further reduced LLM-selected accuracy from 78.3% with history and chemistry context to 73.5% without history, 71.6% without chemistry, and 67.1% when both were removed. These results support the use of constrained LLM guidance as an auditable configuration-selection layer, while cross-chemistry transfer learning and uncertainty-aware EOL prediction provide the experimental setting in which that selection mechanism is evaluated.

items.title: Constructing a Generative AI Framework for Personalised Instructional Resource Development: A Quasi-Experimental Evaluation in a Micro-Lecture Design and Production Course
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is promoted as a way of tailoring instruction to learners, yet most reported applications stay within language and general-education settings, and few measure outcomes in courses whose value lies in design and production skill. This paper describes a four-module generative AI framework for resource development that links learner and content modelling, generation, assessment and community iteration to a course-grounded knowledge base, with the teacher reviewing before release. It was evaluated in a twelve-week quasi-experiment in a professional core course, Micro-lecture Design and Production, at a Chinese vocational college. Two intact classes (n = 45, 44) were taught by the same instructor, who designed the framework; assignment was not random. Covariance-adjusted posttest means differed by 5.6 points (82.3 versus 76.7, p < .001, partial η² = .24), and the framework-supported class reported higher motivation and satisfaction; self-directed learning differed modestly. Preparation time per unit fell by half, though the work became more concentrated and the knowledge base carried a large one-off cost. Because the design cannot separate the framework from the additional resources it produced, the results are framed as associations rather than effects.

items.title: Constructivist Learning in Indonesian Islamic Boarding Schools: A Critical Discourse Analysis of English Lesson Plans
items.abstract: Jean Piaget’s constructivist theory emphasizes active knowledge construction, yet its application in Indonesian Islamic Boarding Schools (IIBS) remains limited. This phenomenological case study examines how constructivist principles are integrated into IIBS English lesson plans using a critical discourse analysis approach. Seven lesson plans from an IIBS in East Java were analyzed over six months. Fairclough’s critical discourse analysis (CDA) was employed to examine power dynamics and ideological influences in classroom discourse within the lesson plans. Findings revealed that while constructivist elements such as problem-based learning, collaborative discussions, and metacognitive reflection are present, their implementation is constrained by hierarchical teacher-student relationships and religious-nationalist discourse framing. Lesson plans encourage active engagement but often reinforce predefined moral and ideological narratives, limiting opportunities for critical inquiry and independent knowledge construction. Despite this, Piagetian principles align with certain Islamic educational traditions, such as ijtihad (independent reasoning) and shura (consultative learning), providing potential avenues for deeper cognitive engagement. This study empirically contributes to qualitative evidence on how Piaget’s constructivist theory is applied within IIBS. This study also offers a practical hybrid pedagogical approach that combines experiential learning with structured guidance, fostering critical thinking without disrupting Islamic traditions.

items.title: Conversational AI in Digital Marketing: Human-Like Interaction, Perceived Empathy, and Customer Loyalty
items.abstract: This study examined associations among Human-Like Interaction, Perceived Empathy, and Customer Loyalty in the use of conversational artificial intelligence (AI) for Indonesian e-commerce. A cross-sectional survey collected questionnaire responses from 300 purposively selected consumers who had experience with e-commerce chatbots or virtual assistants. The analysis used partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) in SmartPLS 4 to assess 18 indicators across three reflective constructs. The reported measurement properties met the specified reliability and validity thresholds. The reported PLS-SEM results indicated positive direct associations among Human-Like Interaction, Perceived Empathy, and Customer Loyalty, alongside a positive specific indirect association through Perceived Empathy. However, discrepancies between the structural model and the direct-effects table prevent a definitive interpretation of the estimated effect magnitudes and mediation type. However, coefficients in the structural diagram differed from those in the direct-effects table, so the magnitudes and type of mediation could not be confirmed from the reported outputs. The study distinguishes perceived conversational naturalness from perceived understanding and company-directed loyalty intentions. These findings concern self-reported perceptions and intentions rather than observed repurchase behavior. Its cross-sectional design and purposive sample preclude causal conclusions and population-wide generalization. The results provide a basis for evaluating interaction quality and perceived understanding in chatbot-supported customer service.

items.title: Critical Thinking and Decision-Making
items.abstract: Working with people requires making thousands of decisions every day—with little help, less time, and often no context. Customer service providers are constantly determining how to respond, what to prioritize, and when to act. The quality of those decisions depends on one’s ability to think critically, reflect thoughtfully, and choose decisively. This chapter examines what research reveals about finding the right balance between reflection and action—when to pause and when to decide, and what questions to ask. It then transitions into decision-making as a structured process, arguing that a good decision isn’t necessarily one with a perfect outcome, but one made through clear reasoning and balanced consideration. Readers will learn to evaluate choices by weighing the long-term benefits, the short-term costs, and the greater good. In its final section, the chapter introduces the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing decision-making. Rather than replacing human judgment, AI serves as a thought partner—helping service providers identify blind spots, test assumptions, and explore alternative viewpoints. Throughout the book, readers will find AI reflection prompts and decision.

items.title: Cumulative damage sequential preventive maintenance strategy for shock resilient machines with prior usage and non-constant shock magnitude
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a modified cumulative damage sequential preventive maintenance (CDSPM) model that addresses the limitations of traditional cumulative shock sequential models by incorporating three realistic factors often ignored in maintenance planning: prior damage in used machines, shock dampening effects and non-constant shock magnitudes. The research seeks to provide a more practical decision-making tool for industries, particularly in developing countries, that rely heavily on fairly-used equipment exposed to complex shock environments. Design/methodology/approach The study modifies the existing CDSPM model by introducing a non-zero initial damage state (R0 > 0), a shock dampening factor αl which is defined as the proportion of shock damage absorbed by the machine. This provides a mathematical mechanism for representing the protective effect of built-in shock-resistance components. The effective shock damage transmitted to the machine is represented by 1-αl100% with 0⩽αl⩽1. This formulation distinguishes between the physical magnitude of an external shock and the actual damage transmitted to the machine. It therefore provides a theoretical basis for incorporating mechanical protection into stochastic reliability models rather than assuming that the entire shock magnitude contributes directly to cumulative damage. Also, the Gamma-distributed shock magnitudes replace the traditional exponential distribution. The modified model formulates total expected cost functions for both infinite and finite time horizons, derives optimality conditions using Lagrange optimization, and develops a comprehensive availability model. The methodology is validated through application to a used Caterpillar 320BL hydraulic excavator using empirical field data, with the algorithm implemented in Python programming language. Findings The modified CDSPM model demonstrates that accounting for prior damage and shock resistance leads to shorter, effective and more realistic maintenance intervals with lower expected maximum cost rate compared to classical models. The optimal policy recommends P* = 12 maintenance intervals with a maximum expected cost rate of 26.99 million Naira and system availability of 98.51%, whereas the classical model (assuming pristine condition) suggests P** = 14 intervals with 58.98 million Naira cost and 99.18% availability for the case study used Caterpillar excavator. The 15% reduction in intervals and significantly lower lifecycle costs confirm the fact that classical models overestimate equipment longevity and underestimate maintenance requirements for fairly-used machines. Research limitations/implications The model's parameters are estimated from a single machine type and operational context, which may limit generalizability. The assumption of a constant shock dampening factor and fixed improvement factor may not capture all operational complexities. These identified baseline conditions are essential for real-world model development. Therefore, future research should explore time-varying dampening factors, multiple failure mechanisms and application to diverse equipment types across different industrial sectors. Practical implications The modified CDSPM model provides maintenance planners with a practical tool for scheduling sequential preventive maintenance (PM) on used equipment, enabling more accurate prediction of maintenance intervals, cost optimization and availability estimation that could not have been appropriate with fixed interval PM. The approach helps reduce unplanned failures, minimize downtime and extend equipment life through evidence-based decision-making that reflects actual machine conditions. Social implications By improving cumulative damage sequential maintenance practices for fairly-used equipment, particularly in developing countries where second-hand machinery is prevalent, the model supports sustainable industrial operations, reduces resource waste and enhances productivity and workers' safety through more reliable equipment performance. This cost-effective maintenance strategy contributes to economic efficiency in resource-constrained environments. Originality/value This research presents an integrated CDSPM model that simultaneously incorporates prior damage, shock dampening and Gamma-distributed shock magnitudes. The work extends Nakagawa and Mizutani’s (2008) foundational model as a special case while providing a more realistic model for used equipment maintenance. The availability model and finite horizon optimization approach offer novel contributions to reliability engineering practice.

items.title: Cyber Security and Forensics with AI-IoT Technologies for the Modern Era
items.abstract: The digital age has seen the sophistication of cyber-attacks increase faster than conventional security control measures, requiring novel and intelligent defense systems. Next-generation cybersecurity incorporates Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in order to enhance computer security with automation, flexibility, and real-time detection of threats. AI-enabled systems are able to run large volumes of data, learn deviations, discover zero-day vulnerabilities, and handle cyber threats with limited human oversight. These smart models keep on learning through the changing patterns of attacks and improve the accuracy and speed with which intrusion detection is done, and reduce the false positives. Artificial intelligence has a role in digital forensics in the automated recovery of data, evidence gathering, and behavior analysis to assist investigators in tracking the digital footprint and creating cybercrime incidents with high accuracy. More complex tools like Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Deep Learning can also be used to detect the unseen links between networks of cybercrime. Nevertheless, AI-driven cybersecurity implementation results in issues of data privacy, the transparency of the algorithms, and the possible abuse of AI by ill-intentioned individuals. The solution to these issues should be a balanced solution that involves a combination of human and smart systems to guarantee ethical and trustworthy safety. In general, AI in cybersecurity and forensics symbolizes a disruptive step to the predictive, self-sufficient, and resilient architecture of defense, and the future of a safer and more reliable online system.

items.title: Data Analytics in Management Accounting: A Bibliometric Analysis
items.abstract: This study examines the evolution of research on data analytics in management accounting by identifying publication trends, influential contributors, collaboration networks, and emerging research themes. Using bibliometric methods, including performance analysis and science mapping, the study analyzes 129 articles published in Scopus-indexed journals between 2014 and 2025. The findings show that the literature is primarily centered on accounting information systems, big data, and artificial intelligence, while machine learning, blockchain technology, and cloud computing have emerged as significant directions for future investigation. By mapping the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of this research domain, the study provides a comprehensive overview of existing knowledge, identifies key research gaps, and proposes an integrative agenda for future research. These findings offer useful insights for both researchers and practitioners seeking to advance the application of data analytics in management accounting.

items.title: Data availability and FAIRness in intervention studies on oral mucositis in children and adolescents: a meta-research study
items.abstract: This meta-research study will assess the availability and FAIRness (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) of data supporting the primary outcomes of intervention studies on oral mucositis in children and adolescents (0–19 years). Oral mucositis is a painful and common complication of chemotherapy, head and neck radiotherapy, and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation conditioning. It can affect eating, speaking, infection risk, and cancer treatment itself. Data sharing in dentistry has been shown to be rare, but no study has yet assessed it in pediatric oral mucositis research specifically. We will run a systematic search, with no language or date restrictions, of MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses. We will include prospective intervention studies, randomized or non-randomized, in which at least one primary outcome relates to oral mucositis. Screening, data extraction, and all assessments will be performed independently by one human reviewer and a generative AI tool (Claude, Anthropic) acting as second reviewer, with disagreements resolved by a third human reviewer. For each study, we will classify both declared and effective data availability, including the data availability statement, access route, repository, identifier, license, and documentation. When data are "available on request," we will contact the authors in a standardized way. We will assess located datasets that have a persistent identifier or resolvable URL using the automated F-UJI tool. Risk of bias (RoB 2 / ROBINS-I) and discrepancies between registered and reported primary outcomes will be explored as secondary aims. The study will not synthesize clinical effects. We expect to estimate the proportion of studies with complete, partial, or no effective data availability and to describe the FAIRness levels of the datasets we locate, including differences between publication periods (up to 2015 vs. 2016 onward). The findings should show where data transparency and responsible reuse can be improved in pediatric oral mucositis research.

items.abstract: Abstract: Title: L0 Invariant State Matrix (L0-ISM): A Deterministic Control Architecture for Critical L0 Infrastructure and Boundary-Constrained Systems Abstract:The increasing reliance on probabilistic Artificial Intelligence and continuous floating-point algorithms in Operational Technology (OT) and Level 0 (L0) critical infrastructure introduces unacceptable risks of stochastic drift, computational latency, and unpredictable edge-case failures. Drawing from the historical transition from additive, zero-less Roman numerals to positional Arabic numerals, this paper argues that modern AI suffers from a structural "Roman Matrix Bloat"—attempting to solve physical control problems by infinitely scaling parameter spaces rather than anchoring value to position and structural equilibrium. To eliminate unconstrained floating-point infinities, we introduce the **L0 Invariant State Matrix (L0-ISM)** architecture—a fundamentally deterministic control paradigm based on discrete positional geometry and axiomatic teleology. The L0-ISM framework maps multidimensional physical and operational parameters onto a rigid, symmetric discrete scale ranging from -9 to +9 using unique, non-repeating positional digits (from 0 to 9), where 0 represents absolute thermodynamic or logical equilibrium (the fulcrum of a balance scale). System states are encapsulated as finite k-dimensional tuples and routed through precompiled Lookup Tables operating in constant time O(1), entirely eliminating computational latency and stochastic uncertainty. The architecture features hardware-level absorbing boundaries at -9 and +9 for immediate interdiction (Hard Stop, -999) and integrates input hysteresis alongside temporal gradients to ensure physical stability against signal noise and actuator chatter. Furthermore, because the state space is strictly bounded to a finite set of 19^k states, the entire logic matrix is natively compatible with exhaustive formal mathematical verification via SMT solvers (such as Z3), guaranteeing the absolute absence of critical failure paths. As documented in early archival records and exploratory working files, the architecture underwent a real-time documented evolution—from early conceptual drafts (Invariant Bytes) to a unified, multi-domain engineering standard. Validated across applications ranging from high-density AI data center liquid cooling (mCDU) to offline transactional edge nodes (Store and Forward T-OTP protocols), the L0-ISM architecture provides a zero-hallucination, fault-tolerant execution engine designed for physical environments where operational failure is simply not an option.

items.title: Debunking Health Misinformation with Generative AI: The Roles of Perceived Authority and Objectivity
items.abstract: Health misinformation threatens public health, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a novel tool for correcting it. Its effectiveness and underlying psychological mechanisms, however, remain underexplored. This study compared generative AI-assisted information verification with search-engine-based information verification in reducing public trust in health misinformation and examined the mediating roles of perceived authority and perceived objectivity across two health misinformation topics. Two quasi-experimental pretest-posttest studies were conducted. Experiment 1 (N = 280) targeted the claim that “blood donation is harmful to health,” which centers on alleged physiological risks of donation. Experiment 2 (N = 232) addressed the claim that “hospice care is equivalent to waiting for death,” which concerns perceptions of hospice care, treatment goals, and end-of-life decision-making. Participants were allocated to either a generative AI-assisted or a search-engine-based information verification condition. Trust in health misinformation was measured before and after the information verification task, and perceived authority and perceived objectivity were measured after the task. Analysis of covariance, hierarchical regression, and bootstrap mediation analyses were conducted to test hypotheses. Generative AI-assisted information verification significantly reduced trust in health misinformation in both studies. Mediation analyses showed that perceived authority and perceived objectivity both served as significant mediators. The pattern of hierarchical regression results differed across the two topics: perceived authority showed a more stable association with trust in the blood donation context, whereas perceived objectivity showed a more stable association with trust in the hospice care context. In two quasi-experimental studies, generative AI-assisted information verification was associated with lower trust in the examined health misinformation claims than search-engine-based information verification. The findings suggest that credibility-related evaluations, including perceived authority and perceived objectivity, may help explain the short-term corrective effects of generative AI in health information verification.

items.title: Decentralization of Artificial Intelligence: The true use of blockchain technology and AI
items.abstract: This whitepaper analyzes the structural problem of centralization in the development of modern artificial intelligence and proposes a conceptual model of decentralized training based on blockchain technology. It examines how the concentration of data, computational infrastructure and models in a reduced number of global corporations creates technological, economic and strategic dependency worldwide. Through progressive examples—from the basic workings of machine learning to the reuse of computations through hashes—the idea of a distributed network (IAChain) is introduced, in which nodes, data, storage and trainings coexist incentivized through digital tokens. The goal is not to present a finished technical solution, but to open a discussion about the feasibility and potential impact of decentralizing the knowledge and processing that will sustain the next generation of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Decolonising Generative AI in South African Teacher Education: Wayfinding for Multilingual, Indigenous, and Publicly Accountable Futures
items.abstract: Abstract This viewpoint article argues that South African teacher education requires a distinctly decolonial agenda for generative artificial intelligence (AI), developed in critical dialogue with scholarship from Aotearoa New Zealand and wider international contexts. AI is not a neutral efficiency tool: its infrastructures, training data, evaluation standards, and platform logics can intensify linguistic hierarchy, data extraction, epistemic marginalisation, and pedagogical standardisation. Drawing on epistemic justice, decoloniality, settler-colonial analysis, and wayfinding, the article synthesises policy and scholarship to develop a framework for multilingual, Indigenous, and publicly accountable AI in teacher education. The comparison is deliberately relational rather than transfer-oriented. South Africa and Aotearoa have distinct colonial histories, constitutional arrangements, and Indigenous political formations; nevertheless, Te Tiriti o Waitangi-informed educational thinking, Māori data and algorithmic sovereignty, and Pacific-led teacher education provide productive tests of whether AI governance redistributes authority or merely adds cultural content to externally controlled systems. The article advances six interdependent propositions: language justice by design; Indigenous Knowledge Systems stewardship; critical AI literacy for teacher agency; assessment redesign around process and judgment; public-interest data governance; and infrastructure-aware inclusion. Decolonising AI, it concludes, is not metaphorical branding or the insertion of local examples into imported systems. It requires material changes to curriculum purposes, decision rights, data relations, evaluation criteria, and institutional accountability so that AI strengthens multilingual participation, community authority, teacher judgment, and public benefit.

items.title: Deep Learning Models for Diabetic Retinopathy: A Comprehensive Review of Detection and Classification Approaches
items.abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a primary cause of blindness globally, mostly affecting diabetics. To avoid irreversible vision loss, DR must be identified and classified as early as possible. Recent advances in deep learning (DL) provide promising ways for early identification and grading of DR sets, potentially changing automated retinal image analysis. This review research examines the deep learning models currently in use for the diagnosis and categorization of diabetic retinopathy. It investigates and evaluates the efficacy, accuracy, and efficiency of various machine learning and deep learning architectures, such as ensemble networks, convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and hybrid models, in identifying DR stages from retinal images and samples. The study also examines the datasets that are often used to train and test these models, as well as the issues posed by imbalance, data scarcity, and the requirement for generalization capabilities in the models. It also examines how DL models may be employed in clinical workflows and evaluates how this might improve diagnostic procedures and patient outcomes. By comparing model performances and identifying patterns and gaps in the literature, this research hopes to highlight areas for future development and the potential for DL models to be a cornerstone in DR screening programs. Through extensive research, this study provides academics, medical professionals, and technologists with a clear route forward for the integration of artificial intelligence in ophthalmology, furthering the process toward more exact, effective, and readily accessible DR detection and classification.

items.title: Deep Learning-Based Fruit and Vegetable Quality Grading Using Computer Vision: Recent Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions:Review
items.abstract: The grading of fruits and vegetables is mostly dependent on subjective visual inspection techniques that require labor. Computers and advanced machine learning systems can help to invent non-destructive tools for quality evaluation of fruits and vegetables based on color, size, shape, texture, ripeness, freshness, and surface damage based on computer vision methods. The paper is presenting reviews of methods used for fruit and vegetable grading, including convolutional neural networks, transfer learning, object detection systems, vision transformers, hyperspectral and multimodal vision techniques, and few-shot learning approaches. The review focuses on grading effectiveness, computation complexity, data variety, and algorithms reliability, and it shows that although many studies report the accuracy level higher than 99% while working with particular datasets, most studies used private datasets, making the comparison of results between various studies impossible. In this regard, the paper addresses the issue of a gap between benchmarks and real-life deployment and proposes a framework based on the grading process that includes a confidence lock mechanism for uncertain predictions and a reliable protocol for testing and benchmarking performances of the algorithms This paper lacks any experimental data as the proposed framework and procedures are designed for future assessment.

items.title: Deep Learning: A Taxonomy and Research Roadmap
items.abstract: This technical report presents a structured taxonomy and research roadmap for deep learning, distinguishing among neural architectures, computational mechanisms, learning paradigms, task-specific architectures, and complete AI systems. The report surveys foundational neural networks, convolutional neural networks, recurrent and sequence-to-sequence architectures, attention mechanisms, Transformer architectures, vision Transformers, generative models, graph deep learning, state-space models, neural differential equations, and deep reinforcement learning. It further examines self-supervised and multimodal learning, mixture-of-experts architectures, meta-learning, continual learning, federated learning, computer vision systems, speech and audio models, time-series modeling, recommendation architectures, metric learning, domain adaptation, knowledge distillation, causal deep learning, neuro-symbolic AI, and emerging neural architectures. The report also covers training and optimization methods, normalization and regularization, large language model efficiency, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, model compression, efficient inference, LLM training and alignment, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic AI, and foundation-model systems. Each major method family is organized around milestone tables, mathematical formulations, and descriptions of its historical development. The report concludes with an overview of the evolution of deep learning, research-oriented mastery levels, and a structured research pathway for natural language processing and large language models. items.title: Deepfake Disaster Communication During Climate Emergencies
items.abstract: Climate emergencies and generative artificial intelligence are creating new challenges for tourism resilience. Deepfake disaster communication, including AI-generated videos, images, and emergency messages, can spread misinformation, erode trust, distort risk perceptions, and disrupt crisis response. Despite growing research on tourism resilience and crisis communication, limited attention has been given to governance challenges posed by deepfake-driven information disorder during climate-related disasters. This chapter proposes the Ethical Governance Framework for Sustainable Tourism Resilience (EGF-STR). Drawing on Situational Crisis Communication Theory, Tourism Resilience Theory, Stakeholder Theory, and Institutional Theory, the framework explains how deepfake disaster communication contributes to information disorder, trust erosion, and tourism vulnerability. It incorporates proactive, adaptive, restorative, and sustainable governance mechanism to strengthen information integrity and ethical AI governance. The chapter provides a roadmap for resilience in an AI-driven environment

items.abstract: The microgrid (MG) operators face significant challenges in effectively meeting power demand requirements, considering the power distribution network&s;s limitations. Furthermore, the MG can use renewable energy (RE) sources to meet the demand response (DR) for customers&s; varying power needs, thereby reducing the carbon footprint. AI-managed, hyper-localized power grids could efficiently manage the intricate needs of a modern energy system consisting of innovative parts like time-varying prices and reliable renewable generation. The present chapter aims to understand the consequences of different perceptions in standalone MG areas. Due to the rising ED and depletion of traditional energy sources and the environmental issues involved in using fossil fuels, there has been an extensive use of RE resources around the world.

items.title: Design and evaluation of adaptive AI-based user experience models for mitigating phishing and social engineering attacks in the U.S. banking sector: A data paper with a synthetic benchmark dataset
items.abstract: Phishing and social engineering remain the main routes to fraud against bank customers. Static warnings lose force as users habituate to them. This paper presents APUX-Bank. This paper is a synthetic benchmark for the design and evaluation of adaptive AI-based user experience (UX) models that defend bank customers against phishing. The dataset simulates a four-arm randomized experiment with 2,400 U.S. adult bank customers and 28,800 message decisions across email, SMS, voice and in-app channels. The four arms are a static warning, a rule-based adaptive warning, an AI-adaptive warning and an AI-adaptive warning with an explanation (AI-XAI). The data were generated from a seeded hierarchical logistic model. Its parameters were set from published phishing research. Logistic regression with participant-clustered errors showed that the AI-adaptive design reduced the odds of clicking a phishing message by 48 percent (OR = 0.52, 95% CI [0.45, 0.59]). The AI-XAI design reduced the odds by 56 percent (OR = 0.44, 95% CI [0.39, 0.51]). The benefit was largest for customers with low digital literacy. AI-XAI also raised usability by 6.2 points on the System Usability Scale and lowered false alarms. Trust in the system mediated 41 percent of its effect on phishing reports. The results held across GEE, random-intercept, probit and linear probability models. A parameter recovery test found that 29 of 31 true values fell inside their 95 percent confidence intervals. The data and all Python code are released for teaching, power analysis and method testing Keywords: Phishing, Social Engineering, Adaptive User Experience, Explainable Artificial Intelligence, Banking Security, Synthetic Data, Logistic Regression.

items.title: Design, Feasibility, and Acceptability of a Neurocognitive and Psychosocial Intervention Module for Drug-Resistant Epilepsy: Findings from a Pilot Study
items.abstract: Abstract Drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) is commonly associated with cognitive impairments and psychosocial difficulties that significantly affect quality of life beyond seizure burden. Individuals with DRE frequently experience difficulties in attention, memory, executive functioning, emotional regulation, stress, stigma, and social participation. Despite the high prevalence of these comorbidities, integrated rehabilitation approaches addressing both neurocognitive and psychosocial domains remain limited, particularly in resource-limited clinical settings. This article aims to develop and evaluate the feasibility and acceptability of a structured neurocognitive and psychosocial intervention module for individuals with DRE. A multidisciplinary intervention module integrating psychoeducation, cognitive retraining exercises, cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), and family counseling was developed through literature review, clinical observations, and expert feedback. The intervention was delivered in eight weekly group sessions in Hindi and English at a tertiary neurology center in India. Ten adults with DRE participated in the pilot study. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, attendance, adherence to home-based activities, and participant engagement. Acceptability was assessed through structured participant feedback regarding clarity, usefulness, relevance, and overall satisfaction with the intervention. Nine of 10 participants completed the intervention. Attendance, engagement, and adherence to home-based activities were satisfactory among participants who completed the study. Participants reported that the intervention content was understandable, relevant, and useful in daily functioning. Cognitive retraining exercises and CBT sessions were perceived as beneficial for improving coping, emotional regulation, and cognitive engagement. Family counseling sessions were positively received and were considered helpful in improving caregiver understanding and family support. One participant reported anxiety related to task performance during cognitive exercises. The findings support the feasibility and acceptability of a structured neurocognitive and psychosocial intervention module for individuals with DRE within a tertiary care clinical setting. Further randomized controlled studies are underway to evaluate the clinical efficacy and long-term applicability of the intervention.

items.title: Designing of specialized language model for medical diagnosis: a systematic review of architectures, applications, and clinical challenges
items.abstract: Abstract Background Large Language Models have become impactful in medicine by facilitating the processing of difficult medical data and aiding diagnosis-making. Given general LLM’s weaknesses, specialized medical LLMs are constructed for clinical precision, contextual understanding and safety in risky diagnostic applications. This review summarizes recent trends in medical LLMs for diagnosis, reported during 2021–2025. Methods A systematic literature review was performed following the PRISMA methodology. A search was designed and systematically carried out in the SCOPUS database using criteria of inclusion and exclusion (type of publication, language, period and country) and 75 peer-reviewed articles were chosen from a database of 1,911 records, after a multi-stage screening and eligibility evaluation. Results In summary, there have been significant advancements in the design and application of medical LLMs, with trends in hybrid architecture, multi-modal learning, prompt optimization techniques, diffusion-based imaging models, and multi-agent diagnostic system models. However, a number of persistent challenges that need to be overcome remain in the development and implementation of these models; namely, hallucination, bias, and poor probability calibration in LLMs, issues with explainability of LLMs, and ineffectiveness in a clinical environment. Conclusions This review highlights the fast pace of development and limitations of domain-specific medical LLMs. While impressive improvements in diagnostic performance have been made, the future directions must address improvements in reliability, safety and clinical validation in order to be seamlessly and responsibly incorporated in the practice.

items.title: Designing sustainable urban intelligence: a green AI framework and survey
items.abstract: The accelerating pace of urbanization has intensified demands on energy, water, transportation, and waste management systems, necessitating intelligent solutions that are both effective and environmentally sustainable. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has demonstrated significant potential in optimizing urban operations; however, the increasing computational complexity and energy consumption of AI models pose new sustainability challenges. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of Green AI methodologies and introduces the Green AI Urban Framework (GAUF), a structured conceptual framework for integrating environmentally responsible AI into sustainable urban systems. The survey examines recent advances in energy-efficient model design, lightweight and adaptive learning techniques, data-efficient training, and resource-aware deployment strategies. Major urban application domains, including electricity demand prediction, water resource optimization, waste management, and smart mobility, are analyzed to identify current capabilities, limitations, and research gaps. Building on these insights, GAUF integrates three core components: sustainability-aware model selection, cloud–edge deployment strategies, and energy-efficiency evaluation metrics across the AI lifecycle. The framework also incorporates implementation and governance considerations relevant to urban infrastructure, sustainability reporting, and municipal adoption. GAUF aims to support researchers, practitioners, and policymakers in designing AI-driven urban systems that balance predictive performance, scalability, and environmental responsibility. By consolidating existing research and outlining future research directions, this study contributes to the development of sustainable AI practices as a core component of next-generation smart and resilient cities.

items.title: DEVELOPER PRODUCTIVITY IN THE ERA OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND MICROSERVICES: A CASE STUDY OF GITHUB COPILOT INTEGRATION AT DUOLINGO
items.abstract: This article examines the real-world experience and results of the strategic implementation of the generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tool "GitHub Copilot" into the development ecosystem of Duolingo – the world's leading educational platform with a global audience of over 500 million users [1]. Amid rapid business scaling, the company faced a critical need to optimize code writing processes. The paper details a comprehensive approach to overcoming cognitive friction and workflow fragmentation that inevitably arose from the evolutionary technological transition of the architecture from 3 large monolithic repositories to a complex distributed network of over 400 microservices [1; 2]. Such decentralization significantly complicated codebase navigation and increased engineer onboarding time. To evaluate the effectiveness of the AI assistant's integration, a multidimensional methodology was applied in the study. Based on an in-depth combined analysis of objective quantitative GitHub ecosystem metrics (specifically pull request processing velocity) and subjective qualitative indicators measured using the "SPACE" framework (satisfaction, performance, activity, communication, efficiency) [6], the positive impact of the innovation is empirically proven. The results demonstrate that the systematic use of AI assistants in close combination with modern cloud development environments (such as GitHub Codespaces) provides a substantial increase in engineering velocity: 25% among developers working in new or unfamiliar repositories, and a consistent 10% in a familiar environment [1]. Furthermore, the article conceptually shows that GenAI tools today go beyond simple autocompletion. They act as a powerful systemic multiplier of team expertise, reduce cognitive load, and serve as an effective means of maintaining mental flow state while solving complex algorithmic tasks [3; 7; 8]. The findings create a scientific and practical foundation for rethinking the role of artificial intelligence as a full-fledged partner in the software engineering process.

items.title: DEVELOPING TEACHERS' PROFESSIONAL-DEONTOLOGICAL COMPETENCE IN THE AGE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: ETHICAL RESPONSIBILITY, PEDAGOGICAL JUDGMENT, AND PROFESSIONAL AGENCY
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI), digital learning environments, and data-driven educational technologies is transforming the professional responsibilities of teachers and creating new demands for ethical and pedagogical decision-making. This paper examines the theoretical foundations of developing teachers’ professional-deontological competence in the context of digital transformation. The study aims to conceptualize professional-deontological competence as an integrated capacity encompassing ethical knowledge, professional responsibility, pedagogical judgment, digital ethics, and reflective practice. A conceptual and analytical approach is employed to examine relevant philosophical perspectives, contemporary teacher competency frameworks, and emerging challenges associated with AI-supported education. The analysis identifies five interrelated dimensions of professional-deontological competence: ethical and normative awareness, value-based professional commitment, responsible pedagogical decision-making, digital and AI ethics, and reflective professional development. The paper argues that effective teacher education should move beyond the transmission of professional codes toward the systematic integration of ethical reasoning into authentic pedagogical situations. It proposes a conceptual framework combining case-based learning, ethical dilemma analysis, reflective practice, and responsible AI use. The paper concludes that strengthening professional-deontological competence is essential for preserving teacher agency, protecting learners’ dignity, and ensuring that technological innovation remains consistent with the humanistic purposes of education. The proposed framework requires further empirical investigation to establish its effectiveness across different educational contexts.

items.title: Development and exploratory validation of the student susceptibility to artificial intelligence (SAI) index among higher education students in Ghana
items.abstract: Abstract Background Generative AI is now routine in student work, yet instruments measuring the risks attached to that use—over-reliance, misuse, and the reflective practices that guard against them—remain scarce in African higher education. This study reports the initial development and exploratory evaluation of a 23-item Student Susceptibility to AI (SAI) item pool. Methods A cross-sectional survey of 408 students, recruited by convenience sampling at six purposively selected Ghanaian institutions, was analysed using a reverse-coding audit, Principal Axis Factoring with Promax rotation, parallel analysis, false-discovery-rate-corrected comparisons and multivariable regression. No pilot preceded the survey, and one sample informed item evaluation and extraction. Results Two-thirds of participants (65.7%) reported daily AI use; only 2.0% none. Parallel analysis supported three factors, the fourth eigenvalue falling below the random threshold; both solutions are reported. Internal consistency was acceptable for Over-Reliance, Cognitive Vulnerability and Resilience & Reflection (α = 0.807–0.824) but inadequate for Misuse/Academic Integrity (α = 0.535), and a total composite was unsupported (ECV = 0.373). Use frequency produced the largest group differences of any variable examined, though adjusted predictors explained only 2.7–7.9% of variance. Conclusion AI use is already near-universal here, so the question is not whether students use these tools but how. Reflective verification practices proved largely independent of the risk dimensions, indicating that susceptibility is not simply a function of use intensity: interventions should target how students interrogate AI output, not how often they consult it. The item pool remains promising but unstable, requiring revision and independent confirmation.

items.title: Development and Validation of the Manual Integrated Ergonomics Risk Assessment Tool (MIERAT): Field Application in a Small-Scale Automotive Service Environment
items.abstract: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders (WRMSDs) remain a major occupational health challenge, and automotive service work is a high-risk context involving awkward postures, repetitive tasks, and sustained static loading. Conventional ergonomic tools capture static posture snapshots and do not reflect how musculoskeletal stress accumulates over time. This study developed the Manual Integrated Ergonomics Risk Assessment Tool (MIERAT), a low-cost, observation-based framework for resource-constrained automotive settings, and conducted an initial field validation. MIERAT combines REBA-based posture severity (PS), exposure duration (D), and a calibrated Time Modifier (TM; 1.0–2.5) into a Cumulative Risk Index (CRI = PS × D × TM), grounded in biomechanical loading theory and aligned with ISO 11226, ISO 11228-1, and ISO 45001. Expert panel review yielded an S-CVI/Ave of 0.95, indicating strong content validity. Duration–CRI associations were very strong for under-vehicle servicing (ρ = 0.910), tyre fitment (ρ = 0.961), and brake/suspension repair (ρ = 0.945), all p < 0.001. Because duration enters the CRI equation directly and also determines the TM, these correlations are mathematically expected; they show that the index behaves as designed but are not independent evidence of construct validity. Inter-rater reliability across three observers was excellent (ICC = 0.975–0.997), with moderate-to-perfect categorical agreement (weighted κ = 0.557–1.000). Task-level profiling identified tyre demounting, wheel alignment, and drain plug loosening as dominant ergonomic hotspots. These findings provide preliminary support for MIERAT as a content-valid and reliable tool for profiling cumulative postural exposure and planning ergonomic interventions in South African automotive workshops. Validation against independent outcomes, such as musculoskeletal symptoms, fatigue, biomechanical loading, or injury data, is needed to establish its construct and predictive validity.

items.abstract: This study aimed to develop automotive occupational health and safety learning multimedia and examine changes in students’ learning interest after its use. The study employed a research and development approach using the ADDIE model and a one-group pretest–posttest design involving 31 Grade 10 automotive engineering students. Data were collected using a 20-item learning interest questionnaire. Expert validation results indicated that the multimedia was highly feasible, with scores exceeding 87%. All questionnaire items were valid, with Cronbach’s alpha values of 0.890 for the pretest and 0.843 for the posttest. The mean learning interest score increased from 70.03 to 86.61, with a normalized gain of 55.52%, categorized as moderate. A one-sample t-test showed that the posttest mean was significantly higher than the reference value of 70 (p < 0.001). These findings suggest that the multimedia has potential to support students’ learning interest. However, the absence of a control group limits causal conclusions.

items.title: Differences in physical and mental health outcomes by occupational type among chinese migrant workers in guinea: a cross-sectional survey
items.abstract: To compare the physical and mental health outcomes between Chinese non-manual and manual workers employed in Guinea, and to explore their occupational profiles. Convenience sampling was used to recruit participants. Data were collected through an online questionnaire survey, yielding a total of 800 valid responses. The questionnaire covered demographic characteristics, self-reported chronic disease status, self-reported infectious diseases history, and mental health status assessed using the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9). Disease burden and mental health outcomes were compared between different occupational groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed estimate adjusted odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals. The prevalence of chronic diseases was significantly higher among non-manual workers than among manual workers (40.8% vs. 27.7%, P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, alcohol consumption, and years of overseas work, non-manual workers remained more likely to have at least one chronic condition. Specifically, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and gout/hyperuricemia were more prevalent among non-manual workers, whereas no significant difference was observed for diabetes. Manual workers had a significantly higher prevalence of previous malaria infection (60.7% vs. 50.7%, P = 0.023), which remained significant after multivariable adjustment. In contrast, the difference in typhoid fever history was attenuated after adjustment. Regarding mental health, non-manual workers had higher anxiety and depression scores. After adjustment, a higher prevalence of subclinical anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 ≥ 5) remained significant, whereas the difference in subclinical depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 ≥ 5) was no longer statistically significant. No significant differences were observed at higher cutoff levels (≥ 10). Non-manual workers reported a higher burden of chronic diseases and higher prevalence of subclinical anxiety symptoms, whereas manual workers reported a higher prevalence of previous malaria infection. These findings may provide useful information for occupational health planning for overseas workers.

items.title: Digital Competency and Artificial Intelligence Integration in Modern Administration: Current Demands, Gaps, and Strategic Pathways
items.abstract: Modern administrative governance is undergoing a systemic socio-technical reconfiguration, transitioning rapidly from manual, paper-bound ledgers and legacy e-governance architectures to integrated digital public infrastructure and Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) co-pilot environments. This evolution demands an expanded conceptualization of workforce digital readiness. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), this study systematically examines the operational demands, capacity deficits, and governance challenges confronting administrative personnel across public sector and higher education institutions, particularly within resource-constrained regional environments. Evaluating an integrated dual-layer competency framework—encompassing core computing proficiencies (advanced spreadsheet manipulation, relational database taxonomy, cloud-based records management, and virtual collaboration) alongside emerging Generative AI capabilities (contextual prompt engineering, automated text summarization, cross-linguistic translation, and critical output verification across platforms such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot)—this paper articulates the comparative operational advantages and structural friction points defining modern public administration. Systemic capacity gaps are identified, including technological anxiety, shallow digital literacy, cybersecurity hygiene vulnerabilities, acute geographical infrastructure disparities (exemplified by power grid instability and bandwidth limitations in regional campus settings), and administrative risks surrounding AI hallucinations and data privacy. To bridge the divide between top-down digital governance policies and ground-level workplace execution, we articulate a multi-tiered strategic roadmap incorporating task-oriented contextual training, robust institutional AI governance frameworks, peer-mentorship coaching networks, and sustained capital infrastructure investments, paired with individual lifelong learning pathways. Ultimately, this research demonstrates that while automated tools and AI engines serve as powerful efficiency enablers, rigorous human oversight, procedural discretion, and ethical boundary-setting remain mandatory to safeguard due process, institutional accountability, and transparent governance.

items.title: Distinct Attention–Behavior Pathways in Neurodiverse Users: An Eye-Tracking Study of Visual Attention to Mobile AR Interfaces
items.abstract: Augmented reality (AR) is increasingly adopted in digital environments to support multimodal experiences. However, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how users with diverse neurocognitive profiles allocate attention within AR interfaces. This study investigates attention and interaction behavior in autistic and typically developing (TD) children (N = 49) using a mobile AR interface. Eye-tracking metrics, including percentage time fixated (PTF) and fixation transitions (FT), were combined with video-based behavioral analysis. TD children demonstrated greater attention to textual instructions and more frequent transitions between interface elements, whereas autistic children exhibited more localized visual attention and fewer transitions. The overall group difference in attention allocation remained significant after demographic and cognitive adjustment, although some AOI-specific contrasts were attenuated. No significant group difference in task performance was detected. These findings suggest distinct attention–behavior pathways, although statistical equivalence in task performance was not established, highlighting the importance of neuroinclusive AR interfaces accommodating diverse attentional strategies.
